title: A free stock research site with powerful tools
author: finshort
selftext:
So last year I created a personal trading tool that fetched data from FINRA and SEC filings in real time. I created Finshort after realizing I could make a free useful product for people based on that.

[https://finshort.com](https://finshort.com/)

It started out as just a short interest screener but it's grown to much more.

The built-in AI only uses the latest official data & filings. It doesn't guess or make up anything like regular AI chat does.  You can also ask the AI on the screener page to find the stocks you're looking for.

Very useful for traders, spot cost to borrow moves in real-time. Insider and Congress trades appear as soon as they are filed with the SEC. Charts with overlays, instant alerts for traders, etc

Value investors can use the screener which has valuation and financial filters and also some value presets. Every stock has a value summary page and a value score calculated from the latest filings. All the data is only sourced from official filings.

Most websites charge money for all of this. No account is required, there's no ads, and the only paid features are alerts and AI because it costs me money every time an email alert goes out and I have to pay API charges for the AI tool. So I can't offer those for free.

If something looks wrong or if you have any feature requests please let me know. I'm a web developer as my main job for 14 years now, i'm still polishing the site every day.

comments.body:
It’s hard to apply AI when there was no intelligence there to begin with.

FINRA data is unreliable and biased. It’s as corrupt as FINRA, a private corporation “regulating” our financial markets. FINRA only exists so lobbyists have a more direct way of screwing our bloated financial markets:

Certain types of Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) data face scrutiny for being unreliable, incomplete, or structurally biased, most notably OTC equity data, TRACE fixed-income reports, and daily short sale volume data. Missing data points are highly prevalent in TRACE securitized products and thinly traded over-the-counter stocks due to delayed reporting windows, volume capping on large trades, and regulatory exemptions for smaller broker-dealers. Analytical bias is heavily embedded in daily short sale data, which only reflects gross transaction volume rather than net short interest and fails to account for market maker hedging exemptions, leading to a skewed perception of market sentiment. Furthermore, self-reported errors from member firms and historical discrepancies within legacy systems like the Order Audit Trail System (OATS)—which has transitioned to the Consolidated Audit Trail (CAT)—frequently introduce anomalies that compromise the data's reliability for precise quantitative research.
